I am an old woman now, fifty-nine years, and I have worked this small piece of land for many seasons. My husband left me this plot and I grow maize here every year with pigeon pea between the rows, the way my mother showed me. I do not have much money — if the coupon from the government comes I will use the fertilizer, but if it does not come I cannot buy a whole bag myself because one bag is too much for my small plot and too much money for my hand. This year I heard the coupon is coming to some women in my village so I will hope and plan small — maybe half a bag of the 23-21-0 at planting and a little urea when the maize is at knee height, and I will put the chicken manure and the ash from my kitchen around the plants like always. I will plant the seed I kept from last harvest because hybrid seed I cannot buy every year, and my daughter will come help me weed when the rains come hard.
